# Baghdad 830 – Scientific method & philosophical ideas

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from eras/islamic-830-baghdad.yaml — do not edit -->

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Scientific method (conjecture, test, publish, repeat)** [`scientific_method`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scientific_method.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Al-Ma'mun's program of new observations to check Ptolemy and the Indian tables is a state-funded test of received numbers, rare in the world. The idea that an experiment decides between theories of nature is not yet stated; Ibn al-Haytham is two centuries away. Local: Yahya ibn Abi Mansur and the Mumtahan (verified) tables; al-Ma'mun.
- **Test claims instead of trusting authority** [`empiricism_over_authority`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/empiricism_over_authority.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Al-Ma'mun's astronomers call their tables 'verified' because they checked Ptolemy, and the Mu'tazila put reason before tradition in theology. In medicine Galen and Hippocrates still decide; al-Razi's Doubts about Galen is c. 900. Local: Yahya ibn Abi Mansur; Abu al-Hudhayl al-Allaf, al-Nazzam (Mu'tazila).
- **Controlled comparison (experiment with control group)** [`controlled_trial`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/controlled_trial.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Physicians test drugs by tradition and on single patients. The bimaristan gathers many patients with the same complaint, the precondition for a comparison nobody makes yet. Local: Yuhanna ibn Masawayh; bimaristan of Baghdad.
- **Placebo effect and blinded trials** [`placebo_blinding`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/placebo_blinding.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low
- **Correlation, causation and confounding** [`correlation_causation_confounding`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/correlation_causation_confounding.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Aristotle's Topics and Analytics distinguish essential from accidental connection, read in Syriac by Christian scholars. Astrologers infer causes from coincidences daily.
- **Selection and survivorship bias, fair sampling** [`selection_bias_sampling`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/selection_bias_sampling.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low
- **Measurement and quantification** [`measurement_quantification`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/measurement_quantification.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. The court measures the heavens, the size of the earth and the Nilometer at Fustat; mints assay coin by weight and touchstone. In medicine dosage is measured, but nobody measures heat, pulse or growth. Local: Ali ibn Isa al-Asturlabi; mint assayers. Elsewhere: Fustat (Nilometer on Roda Island, rebuilt 861).
- **Nature follows simple mathematical laws** [`mathematical_laws_of_nature`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mathematical_laws_of_nature.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. The heavens are believed to move by geometry; Ptolemy is being re-translated and checked. On earth, motion, weight and heat are explained by Aristotle's qualities, not by number. Al-Kindi will argue for mathematics as the way into philosophy. Local: Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Kindi; al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf ibn Matar (Almagest).
- **Falsifiability (risky, testable predictions)** [`falsifiability`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/falsifiability.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. A failed horoscope is blamed on a wrong birth time. Only the astronomers expose their predictions to a check, by timing eclipses. Local: Habash al-Hasib (eclipse computations).
- **Fallibilism (all knowledge of nature is provisional)** [`fallibilism_provisional_knowledge`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/fallibilism_provisional_knowledge.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Kalam debaters argue both sides and switch positions; Greek sceptical arguments are known by report. Revealed knowledge is held certain, and the createdness of the Quran is about to be enforced as certain too.
- **Weighing evidence (base rates and Bayesian updating)** [`bayesian_reasoning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bayesian_reasoning.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low
- **Reproducibility and open publication** [`reproducibility_open_publication`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/reproducibility_open_publication.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept high. Paper and the Suq al-Warraqin make copying cheaper here than in Byzantium or Latin Europe. Translations are commissioned, revised and circulated; observations are written into zijes others can recompute. Knowledge still flows through patrons and teaching circles. Local: Suq al-Warraqin; Khizanat al-Hikma (Sahl ibn Harun).
- **Systematic errors of human judgement (cognitive biases)** [`cognitive_biases`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cognitive_biases.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Hadith critics know that partisanship, piety and invention distort reports. A general account of how judgement errs does not exist.
- **Formal logic (valid deduction and fallacies)** [`formal_logic`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/formal_logic.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Aristotle's Categories, On Interpretation and Prior Analytics are studied by Syriac Christian scholars and partly in Arabic. Kalam debaters use dialectic (jadal) more than syllogism; jurists argue by analogy (qiyas). Local: Catholicos's circle and Syriac schools in Baghdad; Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Kindi.
- **Parsimony (Occam's razor)** [`occams_razor`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/occams_razor.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Aristotle's maxim that nature does nothing in vain is known; Mu'tazila argue from simplicity of explanation as a debating rule.
- **Thought experiment** [`thought_experiment`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/thought_experiment.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Kalam is full of hypothetical cases, and al-Nazzam argues that a body crossing infinitely divisible space must 'leap' (tafra). Mu'tazila and jurists reason freely from imagined cases. Local: Ibrahim al-Nazzam; Abu al-Hudhayl al-Allaf.
- **Source criticism (testing documents and reports)** [`source_criticism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/source_criticism.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high. Hadith scholars judge reports by their chains of transmitters (isnad) and collect information on every transmitter's honesty and memory; Yahya ibn Ma'in in Baghdad is the great critic of men. Criticism of the text itself (matn) is rarer. A player can ride this method into other fields. Local: Yahya ibn Ma'in; Ahmad ibn Hanbal; Muhammad ibn Sa'd (biographical dictionary of transmitters).
- **Consent and ethics of experiments on people** [`informed_consent_research_ethics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/informed_consent_research_ethics.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. The Hippocratic Oath is known to Christian physicians. Al-Ruhawi's Ethics of the Physician comes later in the century. Slaves, prisoners and the poor have no say in what is done to them.
- **Natural causes (naturalism about disease, weather, comets)** [`natural_causes`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/natural_causes.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Aristotle's Meteorology explains rain, thunder and comets naturally, and astronomers predict eclipses. For the Mu'tazila God acts through natures; for their opponents God creates each event directly. Popular belief adds jinn, the evil eye and stars. Local: Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Kindi; Ibrahim al-Nazzam (natures, kumun).
- **Scepticism towards astrology, omens, witchcraft and transmutation** [`scepticism_superstition`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scepticism_superstition.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept low. Astrology is a court profession; al-Ma'mun's astronomers also cast horoscopes and advise on campaigns. Some jurists condemn it as forbidden divination, for religious rather than empirical reasons. Alchemy is a serious craft. Local: Abu Ma'shar al-Balkhi (now a hadith man hostile to the philosophers); court astrologers.
- **Atomism (matter is made of tiny particles in motion)** [`atomism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/atomism.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Abu al-Hudhayl teaches that bodies are made of indivisible parts (al-juz' alladhi la yatajazza') whose properties God creates; al-Nazzam rejects atoms for infinite divisibility. It is theology, not chemistry, but it is the most atomist city in the world. Local: Abu al-Hudhayl al-Allaf; Ibrahim al-Nazzam.
- **The same physical laws on earth and in the heavens** [`universal_physical_laws`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/universal_physical_laws.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Aristotle's heavens are of a fifth element, unchanging and moving in circles; the sublunar world is different in kind. Nobody here questions it.
- **Mechanical philosophy (explain by matter and motion, not hidden purposes)** [`mechanical_philosophy`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mechanical_philosophy.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Greek automata texts entertain courtiers; nobody thinks the world itself works like one. For the kalam atomists the world has no causes of its own at all, only God's habit.
- **Idea of progress (knowledge accumulates, the future can be better)** [`idea_of_progress`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/idea_of_progress.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Al-Ma'mun's men believe they can improve on Ptolemy's numbers, and al-Kindi will say one should take truth from whoever brought it. History is otherwise read as a decline from the Prophet's generation. Local: Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Kindi.
- **Invention as a method (organised research and development)** [`systematic_invention`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/systematic_invention.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept medium. The caliph pays a team, instruments and books to produce new astronomical tables, and the palace library employs copyists and translators. Nobody applies this to machines or medicine. Local: al-Ma'mun's observation program (Shammasiyya 828–829, Qasiyun 831–833).
- **Golden rule and universal ethics** [`golden_rule_universal_ethics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/golden_rule_universal_ethics.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. The hadith that none believes until he wishes for his brother what he wishes for himself is widely quoted; the brother is usually the fellow believer. Christians quote the Gospel version.
- **Human equality and dignity** [`human_equality_dignity`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/human_equality_dignity.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Islam proclaims believers equal before God, and Persian converts (the Shu'ubiyya) argue that Arabs have no claim above them. Law ranks free over slave, man over woman and Muslim over dhimmi. Local: Sahl ibn Harun (Shu'ubi sympathies); al-Jahiz (who argues the other side, and on the Zanj).
- **Natural (human) rights** [`natural_rights`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/natural_rights.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Rights come from God's law, not nature. Jurists protect life and property for Muslims and, by contract, dhimmis.
- **Social contract (government by consent)** [`social_contract`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/social_contract.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept low. The caliph rules by pledge of allegiance (bay'a), sworn and sometimes broken; the civil war of 811–813 was fought over it. The idea that rule is a contract with the ruled is a jurist's theory of later centuries.
- **Freedom of thought, speech and the press** [`freedom_of_speech_thought`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/freedom_of_speech_thought.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept low. Al-Ma'mun hosts debates between theologians and faiths and enjoys argument. In spring 833 he begins the Mihna, testing qadis and scholars on the createdness of the Quran. Open dissent from the caliph's doctrine is about to become dangerous. Local: al-Ma'mun; Ahmad ibn Abi Du'ad; Ahmad ibn Hanbal.
- **Religious toleration and freedom of conscience** [`religious_tolerance`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/religious_tolerance.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Christians, Jews and Zoroastrians are protected dhimmis who pay jizya and stand below Muslims in law; Christians serve as physicians and secretaries at court. Manichaeans (zindiqs) were hunted down under al-Mahdi, and apostasy is death. Local: Catholicos of the Church of the East in Baghdad; Bukhtishu ibn Jibril, Yuhanna ibn Masawayh (Christian physicians).
- **Secular state (separation of religious and civil authority)** [`secular_state`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/secular_state.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. The caliph is the commander of the faithful. The Mihna is precisely the struggle over who decides doctrine, caliph or scholars; the scholars win when al-Mutawakkil ends it (c. 848–851), which separates religious from political authority in practice.
- **Utilitarianism (judge rules by their consequences for everyone)** [`utilitarianism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/utilitarianism.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept low. Jurists weigh 'the public good' (maslaha) and 'preference' (istihsan) in the Hanafi school; never as a general rule above revelation. Local: Hanafi jurists at court (Yahya ibn Aktham).
- **Abolition of judicial torture; proportionate, certain punishment** [`abolition_of_torture`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/abolition_of_torture.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Jurists hold that a confession under duress is invalid, yet police and caliphs flog and imprison, and rebels are crucified on the bridges as a display. Ibn Hanbal will be flogged under the Mihna. Local: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Mus'abi (police of Baghdad).
- **Positive-sum cooperation (trade is not zero-sum)** [`positive_sum_cooperation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/positive_sum_cooperation.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept high. Merchants and partnership law (mudaraba) assume both sides gain from trade; the Prophet himself was a merchant. Courtiers think of revenue as the caliph's share of a fixed harvest.
- **Game theory (prisoner's dilemma, credible commitment)** [`game_theory`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/game_theory.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Chess (shatranj) is the court game and a metaphor for strategy; Persian mirrors for princes teach the calculation of alliances. No theory of strategic choice.
- **Commons problem and how communities solve it** [`tragedy_of_the_commons`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/tragedy_of_the_commons.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Water law is detailed, with rules on shares of canal water, the right to drink and to irrigate, and reserved pastures (hima). Over-irrigation salts the southern Sawad, a commons failure nobody connects to its cause. Local: qadis and canal officials of the Sawad.
